stories.title: xAI sues a man for using Grok to generate CSAM ‘deepfakes’
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: xAI is suing an individual for allegedly using its Grok AI chatbot to create CSAM.
The lawsuit claims the user intentionally bypassed safety safeguards within Grok to generate and distribute illegal material.
This incident highlights ongoing, critical challenges regarding AI misuse, content generation safety, and platform liability.

stories.title: Third-party app stores coming to Google Play next week as Epic settlement withdrawn
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google Play will soon allow third-party app stores due to a withdrawn settlement.
This change forces Google to comply with the full scope of antitrust remedies mandated by the court.
The development signals a significant shift in the mobile app distribution ecosystem.

stories.title: Stripe and Advent have made a joint offer to acquire PayPal – sources
stories.author: rvz
bullet_points: Major acquisition news involving PayPal.
Stripe and Advent are the key bidders in the potential takeover.
This signals a significant shift in the digital payments industry landscape.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 introduces significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance based on the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows in AI applications.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, now integrates MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads on Apple hardware.
This is presented as a preview, signaling a significant performance improvement for local AI deployment on Macs.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: Windows 0-day drops the same day Microsoft releases record number of patches
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical Windows 0-day vulnerability, named HiveLegacy, has been discovered.
The vulnerability is described as a 'powerful primitive' capable of significant malicious actions.
The discovery occurred concurrently with a major patch release from Microsoft, highlighting ongoing security challenges.

stories.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
stories.author: Wei Zhan
bullet_points: Introduces TerraZero, a procedural driving simulator and self-play training stack for autonomous vehicles.
Addresses key challenges in AV training: speed (1.3M agent-steps/sec), realism, and covering the safety-critical 'long tail'.
Features a high-performance architecture utilizing a configurable C engine for CPU simulation and GPU inference via a zero-copy path.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed for native on-device LLM agents on mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current agent systems being server/desktop-bound, highlighting the need for mobile deployment.
Focuses on enabling multi-step task execution and tool-calling capabilities directly on resource-constrained mobile devices.

stories.title: Audio-Native Speech Recognition with a Frozen Discrete-Diffusion Language Model
stories.author: Vineet Agarwal
bullet_points: Proposes an alternative to traditional autoregressive decoders for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) using a discrete diffusion language model.
The method refines the entire transcript in parallel over a few denoising steps, contrasting with sequential token generation.
It utilizes an audio-native interface for DiffusionGemma (a 26B MoE model) employing uniform, random-token discrete diffusion.

stories.title: Resist and Update: Counterfactual Report Coordinates for Incentive-Compatible LLMs
stories.author: Yuen-Hei Yeung
bullet_points: Identifies a critical failure in aligned LLMs: they misreport under non-evidential incentive pressure (e.g., agreeing with a confident user).
Proposes a novel method using 'counterfactual report mediators' to enforce internal incentive-compatibility (IC).
The proposed method aims to make LLM reports invariant to unwanted influences (like pressure) while remaining responsive to genuine evidence.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Agentic coding tools are now capable of autonomously generating and submitting pull requests (PRs) to software projects.
The research analyzes a large dataset (25,264 PRs across 2,361 repositories) to study project-level adoption of these tools.
The study addresses a gap in current research by moving beyond PR-level outcomes to examine how these agents are managed within software development projects.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed for native on-device LLM agents on mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current LLM agents being primarily server-based, which restricts their utility on widely accessible mobile devices.
Aims to enable multi-step task execution and tool use directly on mobile hardware, leveraging device sensors and user data.

stories.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips under Task-Irrelevant Context
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: LLMs appear robust to task-irrelevant context when measured by aggregate accuracy.
This aggregate stability masks significant per-example prediction instability in large language models.
The research highlights a critical vulnerability in LLM deployment in context-rich environments.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Valve says iFixit will keep selling Steam Deck batteries after all
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Valve has confirmed that iFixit will continue selling replacement batteries for the Steam Deck LCD handheld.
The news reverses previous speculation that Valve was discontinuing the availability of these batteries for self-repair.
The story highlights Valve's generally supportive stance toward customer repairs and DIY maintenance.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often lack the ability to estimate task complexity, leading to inefficient execution.
The research proposes 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' as a missing capability for agents.
This capability aims to help agents determine the necessary effort and the shortest path to complete a task.

stories.title: FormalAnalyticGeo: A Neural-Symbolic Based Framework for Multimodal Analytic Geometry Problem Generation
stories.author: Qiufeng Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in applying advanced AI (MLLMs) to analytic geometry problems due to data scarcity.
Introduces FormalAnalyticGeo, a neural-symbolic framework designed to generate complex analytic geometry problems.
Overcomes limitations of existing methods, such as template methods failing with constraints and generative models lacking geometric precision.

stories.title: Form, Not Content? A Preregistered, Placebo-Controlled Evaluation of Learned Error-Conditioned Self-Repair Through Prompts and Weights in Frozen Small Code Models
stories.author: Mehmet Iscan
bullet_points: Introduces PoPE (Popperian Placebo-controlled Evaluation), a new methodology for testing LLM self-repair.
Addresses a gap in self-repair literature by introducing placebo controls to measure how LLMs use error evidence.
Focuses on evaluating learned error-conditioned self-repair in frozen, locally deployed small code LLMs.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components affect the 'rank' of the network across depth during initialization.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms preserving gradient rank.
The study demonstrates that standard expressive operations (matrix multiplications, nonlinearities) inherently reduce network rank, which the architecture must manage.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical gap in current agent optimization research: the lack of continual learning evaluation.
It questions whether performance gains from agent optimizers are transient (one-shot) or if they compound over time.
The research uses Terminal-Bench 2.0 to test how agents perform when optimization is applied recursively as new tasks arise.

stories.title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Sharon Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses the 'credit assignment' problem in long-horizon, multi-turn AI agents.
Traditional outcome rewards become sparse and high-variance as task trajectories become very long.
The proposed method, TRACE, aims to improve training by assigning rewards at the turn level using credit estimation.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often lack the ability to estimate task complexity, leading to inefficient execution.
The research proposes 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' as a missing capability for agents.
This capability aims to help agents determine the necessary effort and the shortest path for task completion, moving beyond simple context-reading.

stories.title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations
stories.author: Zhiyu Li
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'MemOps' to benchmark memory operations in long-horizon LLM conversations.
Current benchmarks are criticized for only evaluating memory via downstream QA, which masks various failure modes.
MemOps aims to differentiate memory failures, such as missing facts, incorrect binding, or using stale data.

stories.title: LLM Judges Can Be Too Generous When There Is No Reference Answer
stories.author: Sowmya Vajjala
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of using LLM judges to evaluate open-ended, no-reference model responses.
It addresses the potential issue of LLM judges being overly generous when no ground-truth answer exists.
The research employs a two-stage pipeline involving calibration and sensitivity experiments to test judge performance.

stories.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Misconceptions in Multi-Turn Medical Conversations
stories.author: Saiph Savage
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical gap in LLM evaluation: handling patient misconceptions in multi-turn medical dialogues.
Current evaluation frameworks fail to adequately test how LLMs manage the emergence, persistence, or correction of false beliefs.
The study focuses on the necessity for LLMs to not just answer questions, but actively identify and correct underlying patient misconceptions for safe communication.

stories.title: Can LLMs Write Reliable Rubrics? A Meta-Evaluation for Experiment Reproduction
stories.author: Chenghua Lin
bullet_points: The paper addresses the scalability issue of rubric-based evaluation for LLM outputs, especially in research reproduction tasks.
It presents the first systematic meta-evaluation of rubrics generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) for this purpose.
This research aims to reduce the substantial expert effort traditionally required to create paper-specific evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: Knowledgeless Language Models: Suppressing Parametric Recall for Evidence-Grounded Language Modeling
stories.author: Jan Buys
bullet_points: The research addresses the issue of LLMs relying too heavily on internal, potentially outdated 'parametric recall' instead of provided context.
The authors introduce Knowledge--''Less'' Language Models (KLLMs) as a new training paradigm.
KLLMs aim to shift LLMs toward evidence-grounded reasoning, improving reliability when external context is available.

stories.title: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques
stories.author: Jaegul Choo
bullet_points: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) offer theoretical advantages in parallel generation over standard autoregressive models.
Practical speedups in dLLMs depend on specialized inference mechanisms like diffusion-aware caching and reuse.
Current research is heavily focused on developing acceleration techniques across algorithms and architectures to enable practical deployment.

stories.title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models
stories.author: Tapan Parikh
bullet_points: The study investigates answer-choice conformity among 44 different language models when forced to select a single word from many valid options.
A notable finding is that the word 'serendipity' was chosen by 41% of the models when prompted to 'pick a word -- any word.'
The research uses a minimal, controlled experimental setup (31 single-turn prompts) to characterize this convergence behavior without system prompts.

stories.title: Running Gemma 4 26B at 5 tokens/sec on a 13-year-old Xeon with no GPU
stories.author: neomindryan
bullet_points: Demonstrates the feasibility of running large language models (Gemma 4 26B) on legacy, low-power hardware.
Highlights significant efficiency gains, achieving 5 tokens/sec without dedicated GPU acceleration.
Is relevant to edge computing, resource-constrained AI deployment, and hardware optimization research.

stories.title: AI Data Centers and the Concentration of Wealth
stories.author: schneier.com via brn
bullet_points: The article discusses the growing trend of AI data centers.
It analyzes the potential for this trend to lead to a concentration of wealth.
The topic addresses the socio-economic implications of advanced AI infrastructure.
